summary: A .js file containing ESM syntax but no "type":"module" marker is now loaded as native ESM (also for require() on Node 24.9+) instead of failing to parse as CommonJS; 30.5.0 narrowed this so such files inside a "type":"commonjs" package or with a .cjs extension throw the CJS parse error as Node does

ESM import attributes are now validated (an unsupported attribute, or a type that does not match the module, throws) and importing JSON without `with { type: 'json' }` prints a deprecation warning that will become an error in Jest 31; before, attributes were ignored and JSON imported silently (30.5.0 emits the warning once per test file)

Importing a CommonJS module from ESM now exposes a broader set of named exports and one shared module instance across importers; the __esModule/Babel default unwrapping 30.4.0 added was reverted in 30.4.1, so the default export is always module.exports as in Node
process.getBuiltinModule() inside a test now returns the sandbox's process and the hooked node:module rather than the host runtime's

Calling module.register() or module.registerHooks() inside a test now throws an actionable error; before, the hooks silently attached to the loader running Jest itself and stayed registered for later test files in the worker

On Node 24.9+, resolution and import-attribute errors anywhere in an ESM graph are raised before any of its CommonJS dependencies execute (Node's run-nothing-on-a-broken-graph order); older Node keeps the previous linking-time execution order

The default resolver now honors the module-sync export condition, so a package exposing an ESM entry point for require() resolves to the file Node would pick instead of failing with Cannot find module
When Node runs with --preserve-symlinks or NODE_PRESERVE_SYMLINKS=1 the default resolver no longer realpaths symlinked modules, matching Node; before it always resolved symlinks to their targets
@jest/source-map's exported getCallsite() is deprecated in favor of SourceMapSupport#getCallsite
@jest/environment-jsdom-abstract (and so jest-environment-jsdom) now declares @types/jsdom as a peer dependency the project must satisfy instead of bundling it as a dependency

reporters, coverageReporters, workerIdleMemoryLimit, cwd and runnerOptions are removed from the project config types and, like maxWorkers and coverageThreshold, now trigger a validation warning when set in a project config instead of being silently ignored
